parts.html: DUMSKAYA DESIGN carries out turnkey renovations of apartments, houses, and commercial spaces in Bratislava, Vienna, and other cities across Slovakia and Austria.

We can take on the entire property — from the interior design project, technical documentation, and cost estimate to construction and finishing work, procurement, custom furniture, and final installation.

We carry out the renovation strictly according to the approved design project: the placement of furniture, lighting, electrical points, and plumbing, as well as the materials, are all defined in advance, so there are fewer changes along the way.

blocks.text: Turnkey renovation with a single team

parts.html: What DUMSKAYA DESIGN can take care of:

items: technical documentation for the construction crew;
sourcing of lighting, plumbing fixtures, and equipment;
manufacturing of custom kitchens, wardrobes, and other furniture;
design supervision of the project’s implementation.

parts.html: You can also order individual stages — for example, if the design project or part of the work has already been completed by another contractor.
Our main types of construction, engineering, and finishing work:
Removal of partition walls, flooring, tile, ceiling structures, doors, plumbing fixtures, and other existing interior elements. Preparing the space for construction and engineering work to begin.

blocks.text: Partition walls and general construction work

parts.html: Building new partition walls from blocks and drywall, creating niches, enclosures, and decorative structures, preparing openings, leveling surfaces, and other construction work according to the project documentation.

Running new electrical wiring, installing and relocating outlets and switches, installing electrical panels and connection points for household appliances, lighting, LED accent lighting, and other electrical equipment.
Laying out water supply and drain lines, relocating plumbing points, installing in-wall toilet frames, bathtubs, shower systems, washbasins, faucets, kitchen plumbing fixtures, and other equipment.

Installing and relocating radiators, preparing connections for heating equipment, installing underfloor heating, and carrying out other engineering work in line with the technical capabilities of the property.
Leveling walls and ceilings, plastering, skim coating, priming, preparing surfaces for paint or decorative finishes, and painting walls and ceilings.
Installation of drywall ceilings, partitions, niches, enclosures, curtain cornices, concealed lighting, and other interior structures.
Laying ceramic and porcelain tile, mosaics, and large-format materials in bathrooms, kitchens, entrance halls, and other rooms.
Subfloor preparation and installation of parquet, engineered wood, laminate, SPC, vinyl flooring, tile, and other types of floor materials.

blocks.text: Installation of doors and decorative elements

parts.html: Installation of interior and concealed doors, baseboards, decorative panels, moldings, and other interior elements.
Installation of recessed and surface-mounted fixtures, pendant lighting, track systems, decorative accent lighting, and LED profiles.

blocks.text: Installation of plumbing fixtures and equipment

parts.html: Installation of toilets, bathtubs, shower enclosures and screens, faucets, sinks, heated towel racks, mirrors, and other equipment.
Design, manufacturing, delivery, and installation of kitchens, built-in wardrobes, walk-in closets, TV walls, wall panels, bathroom furniture, and other made-to-measure cabinet furniture.
Selection and ordering of finishing materials, plumbing fixtures, lighting, doors, furniture, and other interior elements in line with the approved design project.
Installation of furniture, lighting, plumbing fixtures, and decorative elements, completion of installation work, and getting the interior ready for use.

The cost depends on the size and condition of the property, the scope of demolition and construction work, the complexity of the engineering solutions, the materials, the level of furnishing, and the timeline.

For a preliminary assessment, send us a floor plan of the space, a design project, or any existing technical documentation. Based on these, we will give you an approximate cost, and once the scope of work has been clarified, we will prepare a detailed cost estimate.

If there is no finished design yet, we recommend starting with a design project and technical documentation: the renovation budget will be more accurate, and fewer decisions will have to be made on the fly.
